note: `user` IS A REAL NAMESPACE WHEN THE FILE DECLARES IT. The containment and export passes skipped every symbol whose owner was `user`, so a file could not claim a `user` namespace it never declared. But `(in-ns 'user)` DECLARES one, and the definitions after it belong to it: clojure/core/server.clj:169 does exactly this, and its `repl-read`, `repl`, `prepl`, `ex->data`, `resolve-fn`, `io-prepl`, `remote-prepl` and `repl-reply` had no containment at all — 36 real edges lost. The guard belongs on the FALLBACK, never on the NAME; the pair with `no-ns-fallback` is what says so.
